event: At the fourth switchback the stone's voice turns to grit under Wren's boots.
One step is cracked and the next is gone, sheared away into the mist.
She stretches across the gap; the pack pulls her back, then her boot catches and holds.
She stands still against the cliff until the world stops being able to drop her.
Suspended in white mist, she takes the step ahead.
The stair was carved by someone who followed the limestone's grain; she counts the steps.
At the sixth switchback the mist thins and the basin appears in fragments below.
She hears a bird she does not know: three rising notes and a falling trill.
[Wayfinder's Eye] notes moss on the northwest faces, white bell-flowers, worn bands in the steps.
At step eighty-nine a two-meter stretch of cliff face shimmers.
She presses her palms to it: the stone is warm and rings below hearing.
A discovery logs the cliff's sub-audible resonance: +35 XP and an Insight Token.

changes.note: Discovery: sub-audible resonance in the escarpment face

event: At the ninth switchback she almost walks past the Warden's Shelf.
The overhang is three meters deep and eight wide, flat-floored, cupped like a hand.
A rowan grows from a crack at its left edge, where no rowan should grow.
She steps onto the shelf and the cliff's sounds recede behind her.
The overhang gathers the canopy's slow thirty-second breath: the Thornwild is breathing.
[Wayfinder's Eye] is not pulsing but singing; every surface on the shelf glows with attention.
Wren's legs fold and she sits, knees up, and thinks: oh, you're something.
She watches the rowan's leaves turn on the thermal columns and learns their pattern.
She reads the ceiling moss as a map of the stone: +35 XP and an Insight Token.

changes.note: Discovery: moss on the overhang maps the stone's porosity

event: She listens to the forest's breath, ten thousand things breathing at nearly the same time.
A warmth spreads behind her breastbone, like being watched with kindness.
RESONANCE DETECTED: a Sympathetic Bond may be possible; activate [Lay the Path].
She wants the bond the way one wants to open a letter addressed to them.
She breathes in rowan, wet stone and moss, breathes out, and activates [Lay the Path].
She does not dissolve; she sits with the stone, and the stone sits with her back.
She feels the limestone's age as a density pressing into her palms.
She feels the rowan's roots in conversation with the stone over a century.
She hears the breath through the whole curved overhang, down to the bedrock's hum.
The hour passes uncounted; an insect walks the length of her finger.
SYMPATHETIC BOND FORMED: Warden's Shelf, Glimpsed, trait [Sheltered], Slot 1 filled, +50 XP.

changes.note: Sympathetic Bond formed: Warden's Shelf, Glimpsed

event: She opens her eyes: nothing has changed, and everything has.
She stands and feels the shelf in her chest, a second, quieter heartbeat.
Eyes closed, she finds its echo: this ledge, this overhang, this rowan.
ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED: First Step, +1 Attunement: 'You have begun.'
LEVEL UP: Wayfinder Level 2, with +1 Perception, +1 Attunement and three free points.

changes.note: Level 2 reached at the Warden's Shelf bond

event: She puts one point each into Endurance, Pathsense and Dexterity, trusting her body.

changes.note: Level 2 free point placed in Endurance
Level 2 free point placed in Pathsense
Level 2 free point placed in Dexterity

event: Her Level 2 sheet reads PER 11, ATT 12, END 9, PTH 10, DEX 9.
Below the shelf the stair is steeper, and the mist lies behind her.
The stone darkens and streaks with iron; water threads across the steps.
Her road-warden's boots grip wet stone only adequately; she will need better ones.
At step one hundred and sixty the canopy closes over the stair.
The smell hits her: leaf mold, crushed fern, and the sweetness she cannot name.
The three-note bird calls closer, unseen above the green ceiling.
At step two hundred and thirty-one the Shelf's echo shifts from sensation toward memory.
The stair ends, and she stands on the basin floor for the first time.
She finds the overgrown waymarker her father described, its seal under lichen.
She touches it: warm stone, forgotten twelve years, between built and natural.
The Thornwild rises in every direction in green-gold noon dimness.
The air is warm and humid, warmer than any autumn day on the plateau.
Her compass needle will not settle; it swings between two points five degrees apart.
The Thornwild does not want to be mapped, but the Shelf is a fixed point in her chest.
She closes the compass, shoulders her pack and walks into the Thornwild.
